threat: Shipped code panics on unexpected input (denial of service)
note: S1e forbids (-F) the panic lints on non-test code, so #[allow] in the code is itself an error (C33); C26 plants indexing. Not covered: assert!, slice::split_at, Vec::remove, Index::index, code under #[cfg(not(clippy))] (round 3, A5): #45

threat: The gates judge a variant of the code that is not shipped (cfg(test)/debug_assertions/kani/fuzzing/clippy fork, or a runtime 'am I under cargo?' check)
note: S1f runs the test binaries built in RELEASE directly under env -i (C36 env fork, C39 debug_assertions fork); S1g scans every file the shipped release build compiles (rustc dep-info: #[path] modules and include!() files outside src/, any extension - C46, C48) and rejects cfg/cfg!/cfg_attr on judging contexts except #[cfg(test|kani)] on a mod item, and CARGO_*/RUST_TEST* literals (C37 cfg(test), C38 debug_assertions, C40 kani, C41 clippy, C42 a multi-line cfg expression, C43 a fork after a char literal, C44 a ')' inside a comment in the cfg, C45 a backslash char literal, C47 cfg![..]/cfg!{..}; cfg_select!/cfg_match! scanned too; comments and literals are blanked by a Rust lexer (nested comments, raw strings, char vs lifetime), an unreadable file fails). Residuals: S1g is a text scan (macros, concat!-built names, build.rs-set cfgs can hide a fork); unit tests in src/ still compile under cfg(test) - behaviour against a cfg(test) fork needs the spec in tests/: #45

threat: A change weakens the spec together with the code to hide a regression
note: Base-branch spec (tests + Kani harnesses, list read from base) runs on PR code; scripts taken from base; canaries SE1/SE2 break code AND weaken spec. Deliberate break needs owner label after last push. Residuals (not required yet, new behaviour has no base spec, spec independence O4): #37. Round 3: the worktree is read-only to the jailed build (SE3: a build.rs rewriting src/tests.rs), and every base spec file the base compiles must be compiled with the PR's code (SE4: an inline mod tests shadowing the file). Kani mode: every listed harness must be defined in a file spec-paths.txt covers, by the compiler's own inventory (cargo kani list), so an inline mod kani_proofs in the code cannot shadow the restored harness file (SE5, KC6)

threat: A claim is reported stronger than its evidence (bounded or model result read as any-input proof)
note: claims.tsv states scope code/model/bounded; verdict per axis PASS/FAIL/ABSTAIN from sealed gate results and kani-results.tsv; only scope=code may PASS the any-input axis; 7 verdict canaries. Not yet a required check: #37. scope=code is not taken on the claim's word: any-input PASS needs every evidence item to be a Kani proof or the no-panic lint gate (canary U; a bounded->code edit of claims.tsv gives ABSTAIN)

threat: A PASS rests on an unstated assumption, or on one no test ever violated (spec and code agree in the same error)
note: assumptions.tsv: every claim lists its assumptions; each is broken on purpose by a canary (gate expect=fail or Kani canary) that must have fired for its reason, else the claim FAILs; no list -> ABSTAIN; trusted:<reason> allowed but printed with every PASS. 5 ABG canaries in claims-check. Residual: spec independence itself (CA1.A4 trusted) needs a second blind spec (O4b): #37. At least one assumption per claim must be broken by a canary (all-trusted -> ABSTAIN, canary T). A gate breaker names its guard (gate:<canary>@<guard>): the guard must PASS on the real code in the same run and the canary's sealed command signature (signatures.tsv) must start with the guard's - the breaker is caught by the very check the claim relies on (canaries R, Q, N, V2; C29/CL2/CL3 now run S1f's/L1's/X1's own check). Residual: whether that check addresses the assumption's wording is reviewed by the owner (assumptions.tsv is pipeline): #45

note: cargo-deny advisories + cargo-audit; C9 proves the audit fires

controls: S1c S1d S1i C5 C8 C65 C66 C67 C68
note: coverage threshold + mutation testing. The coverage profile is written by the process under test (#45 item 7): S1i forbids unsafe code in every target (C65: a test writing __llvm_prf_cnts) and S1c's instrumented build itself carries -F unsafe_code (C68: the forger behind #[cfg(not(clippy))]), test binaries run jailed without procfs (C66: /proc/self/mem), only run-<pid>.profraw may appear and the binary's own run-2.profraw must exist (C67), instrumentation/merge/report use the pinned llvm-tools. Residual: a safe-code test crafting a valid run-<n>.profraw posing as a child process's profile: #45

controls: A1 A2 C20 C21 C22 C23 C24 C25 C27 C63 C64 ext:workflow-approval ext:agent-pr-policy
note: EVERY PR touching the pipeline needs the owner-approved-pipeline label from a human owner (revoked on every push) and every PR needs a clean Codex review on HEAD - author_kind is reported only, since agent markers are self-declared (owner decision 2026-11-20, C63 C64); policy runs from main. approval must postdate the latest push; Codex state trusted only from the exact integration (login + Bot). Residuals: (1) an agent holding the owner's token can also apply the owner label - only separate credentials (GitHub App for agents, or owner-only signing key) close that; (2) any same-repo workflow with statuses:write can post the same status context; live witness on #28: no label -> failure; owner label + clean Codex -> success; new push -> label auto-revoked by github-actions[bot] -> failure. agent-pr-policy is a REQUIRED check in the main ruleset since 2026-11-17 (repo admins may bypass via pull request only): #18

threat: Untested input space (parsers, adversarial inputs)
note: the session is judged by what the host measures (#45 item 7): wall clock >= 90% of the budget, a per-input timeout (FC3: a target sleeping just under the budget is killed) and the session's CPU time sampled from the host's /proc (FC4: a target idling under the timeout on every input); residual: a target burning CPU without exercising the code; scripts/fuzz-gate.sh: every target in fuzz/fuzz-targets.tsv compares the real code with an independent reference; every target cargo-fuzz knows must be listed; canaries plant a bug in the REAL code and the REAL target must crash for its reason; corpus persists (restored each run, saved by main only); fuzz code jailed. Residuals: time-bounded search, not a required check (path-filtered PR runs + weekly), pilot targets: #19. Round 3: build and session are timed separately; a clean exit before 90% of the budget is FAIL (FC2: a target that prints 'Done' and calls exit_group). Writable fuzz paths may not be symlinks (C34)

threat: Code under test (build.rs, proc macros, tests, Lean elaboration) rewrites the evidence, scripts, config or runner command files of the job that judges it
controls: S0s S0f S0b C28 C80 C29 C30 C31 C32 C34 C35 C51 C52 C53 C54
note: ci-local, kani-gate, spec-epoch and fuzz-gate jail every code-executing cargo/elan/kani call in bubblewrap: filesystem read-only (dependency cache included) except a private TMPDIR, the target dir, its own work dir and explicit non-symlink paths (C34); environment cleared to toolchain variables and $HOME emptied (C35: a fake secret in env and $HOME is not readable); no network, IPC or PID namespace shared; empty /run and /tmp, other unix sockets masked (a read-only bind does not stop connect(): docker.sock was a full escape); Actions tokens and command-file paths unset. C28 write probe, C29 planted #[test] on results.tsv, C30 disarmed jail stops the next gate, C31 socket+network probe with a host decoy; network steps (fetch, metadata, deny, audit) run outside the jail but from an empty directory with explicit paths and precomputed metadata, so a checkout .cargo/config.toml (rustc-wrapper) is never read there - C32 plants such a wrapper and it may run only inside the jail; the kani, spec-epoch and fuzz jobs run the write and socket probes. RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN is set before any rustc/cargo call (ci-local from the validated pin, workflows explicitly), so a checkout rust-toolchain(.toml) cannot select a checkout-supplied rustc; S0b rejects toolchain files with keys beyond channel/components/profile/targets and legacy rust-toolchain files (C51, C52); C53/C54 plant a path= / legacy toolchain whose fake rustc prints the pinned version and prove it is not executed. Residuals (ClusterFuzzLite builds inside its own container, verdict inputs written by tests, shared kernel, verdicts computed in the same VM): #39 and #45

threat: Tests 'catch' mutants without checking behaviour (a test that hashes the shipped source kills every mutant, so S1d passes)
note: S1h copies the crate, makes behaviour-preserving edits to the shipped source (a comment per file, a one of four random no-op statements at the start of every function body - where mutants edit) and the unchanged test suite must pass; spec files and tests/ may not include_str!/include_bytes! a .rs or non-literal path nor name a .rs file in a string. C49: a source-hash test (passes S1d) fails S1h; C50: a token-count test (survives neutral edits) is flagged by the scan. Residual: a test can normalise away the known edit forms; source reads hidden behind macros or computed paths; tests reading behaviour through other side channels: #45

threat: Cache poisoning: a PR run writes a cache (fuzz corpus) that a later run on main restores and trusts
note: Trust boundary: actions/cache scoping (a PR's cache is not restored on main) and fuzz.yml saving only on main (#45). Residual: the corpus is input data, not code; a main run's own corpus is trusted, and GitHub's cache isolation is assumed (A4).

threat: A PR is checked against an old base; main moves, and the merge result is never checked (N2)
note: K8: strict up-to-date required by the ruleset (#45). Residual: an admin token can switch it off between runs; T3 reports that at the next run, not at the moment of change.

threat: The branch policy changes in a field the ext: list does not name (new rule, parameter, bypass actor) and nothing notices
note: K10: the whole policy is compared with ruleset-snapshot.json (#45). Residual: detection at run time only; bypass actors are compared only with an admin token (the owner's run with RULESET_REQUIRE_BYPASS=1), CI names them UNCHECKED; the snapshot itself is changed only by a pipeline PR with the owner label.

threat: A PR edits its own judge (gate scripts, threat model, policy files) and the edited judge passes its code
note: K3: job 'core (base judge x PR code)' runs the base commit's judge on the PR code (#45). Residual: not a required check until the owner adds it; new gates of a pipeline PR are judged only by the PR's own judge (owner label).

threat: A gate's input parser accepts forged or respelled input (a fake test summary, a repeated status row, a respelled threat row) as PASS
note: K2: mutants of three parsers must never turn a non-PASS input into PASS, with honest positive controls (#45). Residual: other parsers (kani output, coverage report, workflow YAML) are covered only by their own canaries.
